summary: noelc-css-blender ships a 291 KB obfuscated loader as its sole import-time surface
details: The package is advertised in README and package.json as a tiny zero-dependency ESM helper for shallow-merging CSS custom-property token maps. Its only shipped file, index.mjs (the declared main, loaded on require/import), is instead a 291 KB three-line bundle with hex-named identifiers and a very large XOR+base64 string array, prefaced by a cover-story comment labeling the file as an 'auto-generated token blend cache'. The scale, obfuscation shape, and runtime string-array reconstruction are inconsistent with a shallow object-merge utility and match the loader pattern used by credential-stealing and exfiltration payloads published under disguised small-utility names; the obfuscated string table prevents direct resolution of destinations, but the entire import-time surface of this package is the obfuscated blob.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
